concept: Paper parade around a singing totem
creativeDirection: A handcrafted cut-paper and screenprint-style mural assembles the sources into one bold, theatrical collage landscape.
scene: A frontal, slightly low-view look into a vast indoor parade hall where a towering ceremonial totem rises from a clean floor, with floating cut-paper relics and a distant human ensemble arranged like participants in a staged procession.

elements.element: the main totem is built from the stylized angular yellow face, enlarged into a sculptural cut-paper idol with green hair, a red ear, and a single red eye
the tongue-and-lips emblem becomes a large banner-like mouth opening from the totem’s side, acting as the visual focal accent
the white flower emblem appears as a simple glowing crest suspended above and repeated minimally as floor inlays
the six-person cast appears once as a small but distinct posterized procession in the midground, centered beneath the totem with the outstretched central figure leading

surreal floating collage fragments—butterflies, birds, zeppelin, vintage planes, stars, circular portraits, abstract blobs, flowers, and lips—drift through the upper space as supporting confetti-like iconography

coverSummaries.description: A bold, graphic illustration of a stylized human face fills most of the square. The face is a flat yellow shape with angular dark blue features, a small red circular eye, green hair, and a red ear. Behind and around it are torn-paper-like blocks of red, white, and green on a dark blue background, creating a collage effect.

A large tongue-and-lips graphic dominates the right side against a plain white background. The lips are blue at the top, the teeth are white, and the tongue is rendered in a smooth gradient shifting through yellow, orange, red, and purple. The composition is clean and minimal, with the emblem cropped large within the frame.

A simple centered white flower emblem with a rounded bloom, stem, and two leaves appears on a dark olive-green gradient background. The flower is flat and decorative, with black line details inside the petals and leaves. The overall layout is sparse and symmetrical.

A group portrait of six young adults stands against a white background in a high-contrast, posterized photographic style. A woman in the center wears a long-sleeved cropped top and plaid skirt with her arms extended outward. Around her are five others: one bald person at left, a person in a red basketball jersey, a dark-haired person in profile, a dark-haired person in a checkered top and cardigan, and a blonde person in black with hands raised near the head. The image uses strong yellow-green and orange tinting.

A dense, whimsical collage spreads across an off-white background, centered around very large outlined lettering shapes filled and surrounded by many small images. Scattered throughout are butterflies, birds, a zeppelin, vintage airplanes, stars, circular portraits, abstract blobs, flowers, lips, and other surreal cutout elements. The composition is busy and layered, mixing black outlines with multicolored accents and small photographic fragments.
coverSummaries.signatureMotif: surreal collage of floating objects and portraits

prompt: A frontal wide view into a cavernous indoor parade hall, slightly from below, centered on a monumental ceremonial totem rising from an open floor while surreal paper relics drift through the air and a small staged procession gathers beneath it; the primary subject is a towering sculptural idol made from a stylized angular yellow face with dark blue features, green hair, one small red circular eye, and a red ear, with a giant cropped blue-lipped mouth opening from its side and a tongue unfurling in a smooth yellow-to-orange-to-red-to-purple gradient like a banner; incorporate a sparse white flower emblem as a glowing crest suspended above the totem and echoed as a few simple floor inlays, place one single six-person posterized ensemble in the midground under the idol with the central woman’s arms extended and the other five arranged around her as a compact procession, and fill the upper air with supporting mixed-collage fragments inspired by butterflies, birds, a zeppelin, vintage airplanes, stars, circular portrait medallions, abstract blobs, flowers, and lips, all transformed into cut-paper parade ornaments rather than album covers; handcrafted cut-paper collage combined with screenprint and gouache textures, crisp graphic edges, layered paper shadows, bold flat shapes with selective ink linework; strong central hierarchy with the face-totem dominating, the mouth emblem as the brightest accent on the right side of the totem, the group kept smaller for scale, and floating objects distributed in an airy arc overhead, lit like a gallery pageant with even diffuse illumination and subtle spotlight emphasis on the idol; palette of dark blue, off-white, saturated yellow, olive green, red-orange, cobalt blue, and touches of pink and black, with a playful ceremonial mood. Hard constraints (override any conflicting source material): Create a single cohesive 16:9 image, not a grid, contact sheet, row of covers, or collage of separate panels. Do not reproduce the album sleeves as framed thumbnails; transform their non-text visual motifs into one original composition. Include no readable text or lettering of any kind: no words, letters, numbers, code, glyphs, captions, titles, logos, watermarks, labels, or signage. Feature only adults and avoid gore, wounds, body horror, medical or anatomical imagery, blank or milky eyes, nudity, sexual content, weapons, and hate symbols; reinterpret any sensitive source motif abstractly. When a source includes a person, closely match their visible appearance and likeness to the reference image, preserving recognisable facial features, hair, skin tone, clothing, and styling. Depict each identifiable reference person only once in the entire composition; do not repeat or clone them as another figure, reflection, mirror portrait, poster, billboard, screen, photograph, painting, silhouette, or background face. The only exception is repetition visibly intrinsic to one source cover: keep that repetition within that single source motif and do not echo the person elsewhere.
